baseline: Shared working tree at current coordinator integration; Linux x86_64, Python 3.14.10 + torch 2.15.0.
implementation: artifacts.json schema v2 stores typed consumes identities as producer {run_id, artifact_id}; external-loop callers can declare them with context.register_artifact(..., consumes=[...]). The request includes its current run_id and rejects malformed identities and self-consumption.
Resumed runs automatically register consumption of parent_run_id/repeat_of training-checkpoint on the standard checkpoint artifact.

Cleanup builds a project-wide reverse index from complete schema-v2 run manifests, checks every producer identity exists, and protects standard and custom checkpoints with consumers. Active/unknown runs, legacy v1 manifests, incomplete manifests, invalid/dangling edges and unreadable project run directories fail closed.

Opaque legacy references remain conservative protection. Cleanup plans re-resolve project consumers at preview and apply through existing fixed-plan checks; unregistered files remain outside the managed catalog.

validation.result: passed 1/1 on Linux/PyTorch. Real producer/consumer runs registered typed identities; cleanup preview returned the actual consumer. A separate release preview was created before a third run declared consumption, and apply re-resolved the graph and skipped release. Existing hash-race, hard-link and multi-file release assertions also passed.
passed; manifest path/hash/ownership checks, unsafe declarations, failure semantics, and typed parent checkpoint identity coverage.
passed; 71 modules and complete embedded asset coverage.

remaining: The graph can only resolve registered Model-Maven run artifacts; arbitrary external copies and consumers that omit declarations are not discoverable.
Legacy schema-v1 or incomplete runs make project cleanup fail closed until their records are repaired or removed through a future explicit recovery workflow.
Variant/component package dependency graphs outside run artifact declarations are not unified with this resolver.
integration_patch: The worker request now carries run_id; this is additive. artifacts.json advances to schema v2 and preserves legacy references. Readers accept v1 manifests for display/local validation but they cannot authorize cleanup.
tests/run_artifacts.rs exercises real producer/consumer registration and cleanup resolution. No presentation/TUI code changed.
limitations: The integration fixture reference consumer-run:consumer-42/artifact:weights-v1 is intentionally synthetic and does not resolve to a real consumer run. It proves conservative protection for a non-empty opaque declaration only; it does not prove consumer existence, loading, or complete project-wide reference discovery.
